title: Conditional Access: which sign-ins does Microsoft Entra allow, and what must users do first?
summary: Hold: authentication contexts are not always inert without a Conditional Access policy. Microsoft documents a PIM fallback that requires MFA when a configured context has no matching policy. The main controls and licensing statements are supported, with smaller corrections needed for documentation differences and checklist coverage.

claims.claim: Conditional Access is Microsoft Entra's policy engine for access decisions.
claims.quote: Conditional Access is Microsoft's Zero Trust policy engine taking signals from various sources into account when enforcing policy decisions.

claims.claim: A policy is an if-then statement requiring an action to access a resource.
claims.quote: Conditional Access policies at their simplest are if-then statements: if a user wants to access a resource, then they must complete an action.

claims.claim: Conditional Access is enforced after first-factor authentication.
claims.quote: Conditional Access policies are enforced after first-factor authentication is completed.

claims.claim: Conditional Access can block access or require MFA, a compliant device or another grant control.
claims.quote: Block access is the most restrictive decision. ... Require multifactor authentication ... Require the device to be marked as compliant

claims.where: What it is: Evaluation comes after first-factor sign-in
claims.claim: Conditional Access is not a frontline defence against DoS attacks but can use signals from them.
claims.quote: Conditional Access isn't intended to be an organization's frontline defense for scenarios like denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, but it can use signals from these events to determine access.

claims.claim: A policy consists of Assignments defining who, what and where, and Access controls defining enforcement.
claims.quote: The assignments section defines who, what, and where for the Conditional Access policy. ... The access controls portion of the Conditional Access policy controls how a policy is enforced.

claims.claim: Policies can target users and groups.
claims.quote: Policies can be targeted to specific users, groups, and agents (Preview) giving admins fine-grained control over access.

claims.claim: Policy assignments can include directory roles.
claims.quote: This assignment can include all users, specific groups of users, directory roles, or external guest users.

claims.claim: Policies can target agents, described collectively as preview.
claims.quote: Policies can be targeted to specific users, groups, and agents (Preview) giving admins fine-grained control over access.
claims.fix: Qualify the preview statement: 'The overview labels agent targeting Preview; the targeting guide specifically marks agent-user targeting Preview.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/howto-target-agent-identities, which lists All agent identities without that marker and All agent users (Preview). Narrow the corresponding Open questions reference to agent-user targeting.

claims.claim: Target resources include cloud apps, user actions and authentication contexts.
claims.quote: Target resources can include or exclude cloud applications, user actions, or authentication contexts that are subjected to the policy.

claims.claim: Network locations are assignment signals.
claims.quote: Network contains IP addresses, geographies, and Global Secure Access' compliant network to Conditional Access policy decisions.

claims.claim: Conditions include sign-in risk, device platforms, client apps and device filters.
claims.quote: Conditions ... Sign-in risk ... Device platforms ... Client apps ... Filter for devices

claims.claim: Access controls can block or grant with one or more requirements, followed by session controls.
claims.quote: The grant control triggers enforcement of one or more controls. ... Once all grant controls are satisfied, session controls are applied

claims.claim: An enforced policy needs a name, users or groups, target resources and grant or block controls.
claims.quote: A Conditional Access policy must include at least the following to be enforced: ... Name ... Users and/or groups ... Target resources ... Grant or Block controls

claims.where: What it is: Everything that applies must be satisfied
claims.claim: Multiple policies can apply to one user and all applicable policies must be satisfied.
claims.quote: Multiple Conditional Access policies can apply to an individual user at any time. In this case, all applicable policies must be satisfied.

claims.where: What it is: Everything that applies must be satisfied
claims.claim: Assignments in one policy are logically combined using AND.
claims.quote: All assignments are logically combined using AND. If you have more than one assignment configured, all assignments must be satisfied to trigger a policy.

claims.claim: Authentication strength is a grant control specifying permitted authentication-method combinations.
claims.quote: An authentication strength is a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access control that specifies which combinations of authentication methods users can use to access a resource.

claims.claim: There are three built-in strengths: MFA, Passwordless MFA and Phishing-resistant MFA.
claims.quote: They can choose from three built-in authentication strengths: Multifactor authentication strength, Passwordless MFA strength, and Phishing-resistant MFA strength.

claims.claim: Administrators can create custom authentication strengths.
claims.quote: They can also create a custom authentication strength based on the authentication method combinations that they want to allow.

claims.claim: Authentication context secures data and actions in applications.
claims.quote: Authentication context secures data and actions in applications.

claims.claim: Authentication context definitions use identifiers c1 to c99.
claims.quote: Organizations can create up to 99 authentication context definitions (c1-c99).
claims.fix: Add: 'The Entra guide documents c1-c99, while the cited beta Graph create reference lists c1-c25 as allowed id values.' Keep both citations: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-cloud-apps and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/conditionalaccessroot-post-authenticationcontextclassreferences?view=graph-rest-beta.

claims.claim: Policies target published authentication contexts under Target resources.
claims.quote: Admins can select published authentication contexts in Conditional Access policies by going to Assignments > Target resources and selecting Authentication context from the Select what this policy applies to menu.

claims.claim: Policies can target registering security information and registering or joining devices rather than an app.
claims.quote: Admins might define a policy based on a user action like Register security information or Register or join devices, letting Conditional Access enforce controls around those actions.

claims.claim: Report-only evaluates and logs policies without enforcing them.
claims.quote: During sign-in, the system evaluates policies in report-only mode but doesn't enforce them. Results are logged in the Conditional Access and Report-only tabs of the Sign-in log details.

claims.claim: The Coverage tab shows which apps have Conditional Access policy coverage.
claims.quote: The Coverage tab shows a summary of applications with and without Conditional Access policy coverage over the past seven days.

claims.claim: An app with no applicable policy does not receive a Conditional Access access-control decision.
claims.quote: Access tokens are issued by default if a Conditional Access policy condition doesn't trigger an access control. This policy doesn't prevent the app from blocking access on its own.

claims.claim: Security defaults are available to customers without Conditional Access licences.
claims.quote: Customers without licenses that include Conditional Access can make use of security defaults to block legacy authentication.

claims.claim: Conditional Access requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 licences.
claims.quote: Using this feature requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses.
claims.fix: Retain the general P1 requirement, but add to Cost and licensing: 'For agent policies, Microsoft's licensing page additionally requires Microsoft 365 E7, or Microsoft Agent 365 paired with at least Microsoft Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3.' Add https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/fundamentals/licensing to sources; it gives these additional requirements whereas the overview gives the general P1 requirement.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Business Premium customers can use Conditional Access features.
claims.quote: Customers with Microsoft 365 Business Premium licenses can also use Conditional Access features.

claims.claim: Sign-in-risk and user-risk policies require ID Protection, a Microsoft Entra ID P2 feature.
claims.quote: Risk-based Conditional Access policies (sign-in risk and user risk) require Microsoft Entra ID Protection, which is a Microsoft Entra ID P2 feature.

claims.claim: Interacting products including Workload ID, Intune and Purview require their appropriate licences.
claims.quote: Other products and features that interact with Conditional Access policies require appropriate licensing for those products and features, including Microsoft Entra Workload ID, Microsoft Entra ID Protection, Microsoft Intune, and Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Licence expiry does not automatically disable or delete Conditional Access policies.
claims.quote: When the licenses required for Conditional Access expire, policies aren't automatically disabled or deleted.

claims.claim: After licence expiry remaining policies can be viewed and deleted but not updated.
claims.quote: You can view and delete remaining policies, but you can't update them.

claims.claim: The Conditional Access Optimization Agent needs at least P1 and Security Copilot SCUs.
claims.quote: The Conditional Access Optimization Agent with Microsoft Security Copilot ... The agent needs at least the Microsoft Entra ID P1 license and security compute units (SCU).

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate meter or per-policy charge for Conditional Access itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Conditional Access pricing separate per policy charge meter Entra ID P1 licensing. Opened Conditional Access overview and Entra fundamentals/licensing; reviewed licensing search results. They name licence requirements, not a Conditional Access per-policy meter.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Lockout
claims.claim: Combining a block policy with All resources can lock out administrators.
claims.quote: Be careful when using block and all resources in a single policy. This combination could lock out admins

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends excluding emergency access accounts and at least one account to prevent lockout.
claims.quote: Emergency access or break-glass accounts to prevent lockout due to policy misconfiguration. ... Microsoft recommends you exclude at least one account to prevent yourself from being locked out due to misconfiguration.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Report-only is not a full dry run
claims.claim: Report-only policies do not prompt for MFA.
claims.quote: Users aren't prompted for multifactor authentication or blocked by report-only policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Report-only is not a full dry run
claims.claim: Report-only policies do not prompt users to satisfy terms of use.
claims.quote: With report-only mode, the user isn't prompted to satisfy the required controls. For example, users aren't prompted for multifactor authentication challenges or terms of use.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Report-only is not a full dry run
claims.claim: Report-only cannot evaluate policies in the User Actions scope.
claims.quote: Administrators can evaluate Conditional Access policies in report-only mode, except for items included in the "User Actions" scope.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Report-only is not a full dry run
claims.claim: Report-only compliant-device policies can prompt macOS, iOS and Android users to select a certificate.
claims.quote: Policies in report-only mode that require a compliant device can prompt users on macOS, iOS, and Android devices to select a device certificate during policy evaluation, even though device compliance isn't enforced.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group and role changes lag
claims.claim: Policies targeting roles or groups are evaluated only when a token is issued.
claims.quote: Policies targeting roles or groups are evaluated only when a token is issued.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group and role changes lag
claims.claim: Newly added role or group members are not subject to the policy until they get a new token.
claims.quote: Newly added users to a role or group aren't subject to the policy until they get a new token.

claims.where: Risks and limits: User-scoped policies do not cover service principals
claims.claim: User-scoped Conditional Access policies do not block service-principal calls.
claims.quote: Calls made by service principals aren't blocked by Conditional Access policies scoped to users.

claims.where: Risks and limits: User-scoped policies do not cover service principals
claims.claim: Conditional Access for workload identities defines policies targeting service principals.
claims.quote: Use Conditional Access for workload identities to define policies that target service principals.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Device platform is weak evidence
claims.claim: Device platform is derived from unverified information such as changeable user agent strings.
claims.quote: The information used to determine the device platform comes from unverified sources, like user agent strings that can be changed.

claims.claim: Require MFA and Require authentication strength cannot be combined in one policy.
claims.quote: You can't use the Require multifactor authentication and Require authentication strength grant controls together in the same Conditional Access policy.

claims.where: Risks and limits: All resources reaches account recovery
claims.claim: All resources policies cover onboarding and account recovery unless the global exclusion is enabled.
claims.quote: Policies targeting All resources also apply to onboarding and account recovery events unless you enable the global user-action exclusion.

claims.where: Risks and limits: All resources reaches account recovery
claims.claim: Those policies can require credentials users cannot yet provide during onboarding or recovery.
claims.quote: These policies can require credentials or other controls that users can't satisfy before they establish or restore their authentication methods.

claims.claim: The tenant policy limit is 240, including On, Off and Report-only policies.
claims.quote: Conditional Access has a limit of 240 policies per tenant. This 240-policy limit includes Conditional Access policies in any state, including report-only mode, on, or off.

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy reaches policy creation.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies. Select New policy. ... Under Access controls > Grant, select Block access.
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct form but stops before the grant/block control. Give the remaining route in the note: 'Configure policy assignments in New policy; the block control is at Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy > Access controls > Grant > Block access.'

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/identity/conditionalAccess/policies creates a policy with targeting and grant or block controls.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/identity/conditionalAccess/policies ... "conditions": { ... "grantControls": { "operator": "OR", "builtInControls": [ "mfa" ] }
claims.fix: Keep the call and add to controls[0].note: 'The request body sets conditions for targeting and grantControls for grant or block requirements.' The cited conditionalAccessPolicy resource documents both properties.

claims.claim: Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy > Enable policy reaches the policy-state control.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies. Select New policy. ... set Enable policy to Report-only. ... move the Enable policy toggle from Report-only to On.

claims.claim: The state property accepts enabled, disabled and enabledForReportingButNotEnforced.
claims.quote: Specifies the state of the conditionalAccessPolicy object. The possible values are: enabled, disabled, enabledForReportingButNotEnforced. Required.

claims.claim: The allowedCombinations request-body property defines accepted authentication combinations.

claims.claim: Built-in authentication strengths cannot be modified.

claims.claim: Entra ID > Conditional Access > Authentication context > New authentication context reaches context-definition creation.

claims.claim: Security Reader can view Conditional Access.

claims.claim: The policy creation guide requires at least Conditional Access Administrator.

claims.claim: The custom-strength guide requires at least Security Administrator.

claims.quote: This operation supports the following built-in roles ... Conditional Access administrator ... Security Administrator

claims.quote: The policy impact view of Conditional Access lets admins with at least the Security Reader role see a snapshot of the potential or existing impacts of policies on interactive sign-ins in your organization.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: On enforces policies, Report-only evaluates without enforcement and Off prevents application.
claims.quote: move the Enable policy toggle from Report-only to On. ... Disabling a policy makes sure it doesn't apply when a user tries to sign in.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: The Conditional Access Insights and Reporting workbook visualizes policy results including report-only results.
claims.quote: Use the Conditional Access Insights and Reporting workbook to view report-only and enforced policy results side by side for a specific time range, set of applications, and users.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact

claims.quote: The workbook requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 and a Log Analytics workspace that's receiving sign-in logs

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact

claims.claim: Authentication strengths need a policy reference to enforce their requirements.

claims.claim: Authentication contexts do nothing until a policy references them.
claims.quote: if there are no Conditional Access policies in the tenant that target authentication context configured in PIM settings, during group membership/ownership activation, the multifactor authentication feature in Microsoft Entra ID is required
claims.fix: Remove 'and contexts' from 'Authentication strengths and contexts do nothing until a policy references them.' Microsoft documents a PIM MFA fallback when a configured context has no matching Conditional Access policy, so the unconditional statement about contexts is false.

claims.claim: Authentication context applies to custom, line-of-business, SharePoint and Defender for Cloud Apps-protected applications.
claims.quote: These applications include custom applications, line-of-business (LOB) applications, SharePoint, or applications protected by Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.

claims.claim: The Account onboarding and recovery global exclusion is marked preview.
claims.quote: Exclude onboarding and recovery from All resources policies (preview) ... Account onboarding and recovery (Preview) setting.

claims.claim: Learn gives no general-availability date for the agent-targeting preview.
claims.quote: Searched: Conditional Access agent targeting preview generally available November 2026. Opened overview, agent-id and howto-target-agent-identities; no GA date found. The targeting guide specifically labels agent-user targeting Preview; the broader wording is corrected with the preview claim.

claims.claim: Learn gives no general-availability date for the global onboarding and recovery exclusion.
claims.quote: Searched: Conditional Access agent targeting account onboarding recovery exclusion policy impact preview general availability date. Opened Target resources and read Require identity verification search excerpts; no GA date for the exclusion found.

claims.claim: Learn gives no general-availability date for policy impact.
claims.quote: Searched: Conditional Access agent targeting account onboarding recovery exclusion policy impact preview general availability date. Opened Analyze Conditional Access Policy Impact and read its search results; it labels policy impact preview without a GA date.
